title: Wavefront NCCl overlap orchestrator and kernel-routing for balanced multi-GPU prefill/decode
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation:
Current multi-GPU prefill/decode paths suffer from throughput variance and tail latency spikes when token-wave arrivals coincide with large collective ops (NCCL). Kernel selection heuristics are currently per-device and static for a model variant; they don’t account for cross-device comm windows or token-wave density. This ticket explores a wavefront-driven orchestration layer that coordinates NCCL windows, microbatch placement, and per-stage kernel hints to increase NCCL overlap without regressing median latency or model quality.

Goals / Success criteria:
- Reduce end-to-end 95th percentile latency for prefill+decode by 18% for 8-GPU device pools on representative workloads (chatty 32-token prompts and long-context 4096 prefills).
- Keep median latency within 5% of baseline.
- Improve NCCL utilization overlap measured as percent of time GPU compute is active during collective phases by at least 20 percentage points.
- No increase in sampling/regeneration artifacts due to kernel changes (quality regression < 0.5% measured by existing eval prompts).

Scope and constraints:
- Target: tensor-parallel + pipeline-parallel mixes used by production models (TP=2..8, PP=1..4).
- Must be compatible with Dedicated clusters (no privileged infra changes).
- Rollout via runtime-1.22 feature flag; default off for Canary customers.

Design overview:
1) Wavefront coordinator: lightweight controller that observes token arrival timestamps (microbatch boundaries) and exposes a short-horizon schedule (50-200ms) for when to trigger bulk NCCL collectives vs. staggered small collectives. The schedule is 'advisory' to stage executors and encoded as sequence of epoch tokens.
2) Microbatch placement policy: prefer grouping prefill microbatches that reduce cross-stage stragglers; use per-device queuing metrics to place hot microbatches in staggered windows to maximize overlap.
3) Kernel-routing hints: runtime emits kernel preference tags per attention layer (e.g., fused-atten-fast, sparse-attn-hint, kvcache-shared) based on sequence-length distribution and current wavefront schedule. Stage executors select kernels with a soft-budget model (latency vs. comm size).
4) NCCL overlap windows: instead of one big collective at prefill barrier, allow controlled piecemeal collectives aligned to token-wavefronts to permit compute/comm overlap. Windows are parameterized by max-slice-size and min-interference gap so small collectives can run without blocking critical path kernels.

Trade-offs considered:
- Larger piecemeal collectives increase NCCL startup overhead but enable compute overlap. We’ll tune slice size to balance overhead vs. overlap gains per hardware class.
- Kernel switching adds complexity and may increase instruction cache churn; mitigations: hysteresis, per-layer cooldown, and telemetry to roll back.
- Advisory schedule vs. strict barrier: advisory design chosen to avoid global stalls from clock sync issues and to allow device-local opportunistic work.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1 (Feb 15-21): PoC coordinator proto in runtime (observability hooks, simple wavefront trigger). Bench microbench harness against 8x A100 pool.
- Week 2: Implement microbatch placement and NCCL slice plumbing in executor. Add kernel-routing hint infrastructure.
- Week 3: Run integration perf sweep and quality evals. Collect telemetry hooks for per-layer latency histograms and NCCL occupancy.
- Week 4: Canary rollout behind feature flag + safety fallback (automatic revert if 95th latency increases >10%).

Testing and validation:
- Synthetic perf matrix: varying TP/PP, seq_len in {256,1024,4096}, microbatch sizes {1,4,8} across 8-GPU and 4-GPU pools.
- Regression evals: existing prompt suite (n=5k) + targeted attention-sensitive prompts.
- Chaos tests: simulated slow device (50ms slow) to validate graceful degradation and fallback to barrier mode.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- New Grafana panel: nccl_overlap_percent, kernel_switch_rate, wavefront_miss_rate. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/runtime/wavefront-overlap (internal).
- Perf PRG: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1426 (WIP branch).

Open questions / risks:
- Does increased NCCL concurrency exacerbate PCIe saturation on multi-socket nodes? Need hw team input.
- Kernel selection policy must not impact numerical determinism guarantees; check FP32->FP16 codepaths.
- Impact on Dedicated customers with strict capacity isolation: ensure feature flag and rollout controls.

Rollout and follow-ups:
- Canary with low-traffic Dedicated tenants; gather 7-day rolling metrics.
- If stable, enable for Dedicated low-priority pool then gradually for default pool.
- Post-rollout: auto-tuning agent task to adapt slice-size per cluster and per-model.

comments: 2026-02-16 - Ava Chen: Initial spike completed. Coordinator prototype emits wavefront epochs and reduces false-positive stalling by 30% in microbench harness. Saved logs to /tmp/wavefront-spike-20260216.tar.gz (internal).

2026-02-20 - Marcus Rivera: Implemented NCCL slice plumbing and a first pass of kernel hints. Observed 12% improvement in NCCL overlap on 8xA100 but a 3% median latency regression for short prompts. Added hysteresis variables to kernel selector to reduce oscillation.

2026-02-26 - Infra: Asked for PCIe utilization traces during piecemeal collectives. Triggered hardware dive; no immediate saturation on test nodes but need broader sampling. Action: coordinate with hw-team (owner: Priya Gupta).

2026-03-02 - QA: Ran regression evals; quality delta <0.2% for sampled prompts. Chaos test with simulated slow device: coordinator gracefully reverted to barrier mode after 6 consecutive missed epochs. Added safety metric to auto-fallback if wavefront_miss_rate > 0.15.

2026-03-05 - Marcus Rivera: Preparing canary rollout plan and adding feature-flag config in runtime flags: runtime.wavefront_orchestrator.enabled and runtime.wavefront_orchestrator.slice_size_hint. Next: add canary config and revert playbook.
